top_pick.title: Diagnostic-code registry coherence (emit ⊆ declared, declared ⊆ emitted, pinned ⊆ declared)
top_pick.why: Highest (value × buildability) and the single most-corroborated invariant in the sweep — FOUR lenses (two_source_drift.1, two_source_drift.4, unenforced_convention.1, unenforced_convention.3/dangerous_change_shape.3) independently walked into the same file, src/errors.zig. It exercises the rail cleanly: a deterministic three-set FACT scan over a closed registry, with a real violation on BOTH primary arms verified live (KORU200 emitted-but-undeclared at main.zig:3604; 11 declared-but-dead codes), and a clean control arm (test pins all resolve today, so the pinned-arm stays silent now and only fires on a future rename). The dead-code arm is the one place a judge earns its keep — distinguishing a genuinely-reserved code from a forgotten one — so it also demos the fact×intent product gate, while the orphan-emit and rotten-pin arms are pure mechanical set-difference. One engine, four lenses, two live anchors, one clean control.
top_pick.build_sketch: FACT scan (no LLM): (1) DECLARED = parse members from the `pub const ErrorCode = enum(u16)` block in src/errors.zig:3-86. (2) EMITTED = union of (a) regex `error\[([A-Z]+[0-9]+)\]` raw string literals across src/**.zig, and (b) `\.((KORU|PARSE|TYPE|SHAPE)[0-9]+)\b` enum-tag uses across src/ + koru_std/, minus the errors.zig declaration lines themselves. (3) PINNED = `(KORU|PARSE|TYPE|SHAPE)[0-9]{3}` over tests/regression/**/{EXPECT,expected*.txt}. Emit three diffs: ORPHAN_EMIT=EMITTED\DECLARED, DEAD=DECLARED\EMITTED, ROTTEN_PIN=PINNED\DECLARED. JUDGE axis (gates ONLY the DEAD arm): code_is_aspirational ∈[-1,1] — +1 the enum line carries an explicit reserved/aspirational comment, -1 a code sits with zero emit sites under no such marker. PRODUCT GATE: ORPHAN_EMIT and ROTTEN_PIN fire pure-FACT (set-diff >= 1, deterministic, no judge). DEAD fires = FACT(DEAD grows on this diff) × INTENT(code_is_aspirational <= -0.5) × gain >= floor. ANCHOR it must fire on: HEAD state — ORPHAN_EMIT={KORU200} (main.zig:3604) and DEAD={KORU031,KORU042,KORU043,KORU052,KORU060,KORU061,KORU070,KORU082,KORU090,KORU091,PARSE002}. CONTROL it must stay silent on: KORU030 (36 emit sites) and KORU034 (1 site) — both declared AND emitted; and the current PINNED set, which fully resolves into DECLARED today, so ROTTEN_PIN=∅ until a future rename. A benign enum reorder/rename that preserves all three set-memberships scores every diff empty and stays silent.

commission_queue.title: Diagnostic-code registry coherence: emit ⊆ declared, declared ⊆ emitted, pinned ⊆ declared
commission_queue.intent: Keep src/errors.zig the honest single source of truth for diagnostics: no code emitted that isn't declared, no code declared that's never emitted (a lie that claims the compiler catches something it doesn't), no test pinned to a code that can't fire.
commission_queue.faucet: FACT (three sets, one scan): EMITTED = raw `error\[([A-Z]+[0-9]+)\]` string literals across src/ PLUS `.KORU###`/`.PARSE###`/etc enum-tag uses; DECLARED = enum members parsed from the `pub const ErrorCode = enum` block in src/errors.zig; PINNED = codes referenced in tests/**/{EXPECT,expected*.txt}. Emit the three set-differences: EMITTED\DECLARED (orphan emits), DECLARED\EMITTED (dead codes), PINNED\DECLARED (rotten pins). INTENT (only to gate the dead-code arm): axis code_is_aspirational: +1 a newly-added enum member is marked reserved/aspirational with a comment, -1 a code is added or left with zero emit sites under no such marker.
commission_queue.gate: Two arms. Pure-FACT arm (no judge): fire if EMITTED\DECLARED >= 1 OR PINNED\DECLARED >= 1 — a closed-registry set difference, deterministic. Dead-code arm: fire = FACT(DECLARED\EMITTED introduced/grows by this diff) × INTENT(code_is_aspirational <= -0.5) × gain >= floor, so a benign reserved-code addition stays silent.
commission_queue.fires_on: TODAY: EMITTED\DECLARED = {KORU200} (src/main.zig:3604, verified absent from enum at src/errors.zig:3-86). DECLARED\EMITTED = {KORU031,KORU042,KORU043,KORU052,KORU060,KORU061,KORU070,KORU082,KORU090,KORU091,PARSE002} — 11 codes with emit_sites=0, verified by grep. Also fires on a future rename like KORU044→KORU047 that leaves the 8 expected.txt pins dangling.

commission_queue.title: Product version is one number across all five sites
commission_queue.intent: A release has exactly one version; `koruc --version`, the manifest, the scaffolded-project templates, the CCP handshake, and the CHANGELOG must agree.
commission_queue.faucet: FACT: collect version strings from src/main.zig `const version`, koru.json `.version`, the newest `## [X.Y.Z]` CHANGELOG header, and the hardcoded `"version": "X.Y.Z"` literals in ccp.zig + project_template.zig; whitelist build.zig.zon's `0.0.0` (documented Zig package-dedup placeholder). Returns the distinct release-version set and whether main.zig's version has a matching CHANGELOG header.
commission_queue.gate: Pure FACT: fire = count(distinct non-placeholder versions) > 1 OR main.zig version has no `## [that-version]` CHANGELOG header. No judge.

commission_queue.title: canonicalize post-condition: every DottedPath gets a module_qualifier, no silent null-skip downstream
commission_queue.intent: The documented post-condition of canonicalize_names (every DottedPath has module_qualifier != null) must stay enforced as the AST grows, and consumers must assert it rather than silently papering over a null with `orelse`/`if(mq)`.
commission_queue.faucet: FACT: AST-walk — enumerate every ast.Item/ast.Step variant that (transitively) holds a DottedPath field (grep ast.zig: `:\s*\??\[?\]?DottedPath` → ~15 fields), check each is reached by a canonicalizePath call in the src/canonicalize_names.zig walker; return count of uncovered path-bearing variants. INTENT axis path_coverage_complete: +1 a diff adding a path-bearing AST variant adds the matching walker call (or a justified skip), -1 it adds the variant with no walker edit; axis fallback_masks_invariant: +1 a downstream module_qualifier read asserts non-null, -1 it adds another silent `orelse`/`if(mq)`.
commission_queue.gate: fire = FACT(uncovered path-bearing variants >= 1, i.e. a new variant added without a walker edit) × INTENT(path_coverage_complete <= -0.5) × gain >= floor. A benign walker rename/reorder keeps coverage at full → FACT=0 → silent.
commission_queue.fires_on: FUTURE: a commit adding an ast.Item/ast.Step variant carrying a DottedPath without touching canonicalize_names.zig — the path keeps module_qualifier==null and continuation_codegen.zig:31 (`if (invocation.path.module_qualifier) |mq| {...}`, verified) silently emits a bare unqualified symbol, surfacing 3 steps later as a wrong-module/unknown-symbol error in generated Zig.

commission_queue.title: No orphaned expected.txt that degrades to a false-green compile-only test
commission_queue.intent: A regression dir shipping expected.txt must carry a run/assert marker (MUST_RUN or EXPECT), or its expected output is never compared and the test silently passes the moment it compiles.
commission_queue.faucet: FACT: walk tests/regression/**; flag dirs with expected.txt present, no MUST_RUN, no EXPECT. Return paths plus their SUCCESS/FAILURE marker state.
commission_queue.gate: Pure FACT with a product-anchor clause: fire = (dir has expected.txt) AND NOT(MUST_RUN OR EXPECT) AND (SUCCESS present, no FAILURE). The SUCCESS-without-FAILURE clause isolates the dangerous false-green subset from merely-deferred TODOs.
commission_queue.fires_on: LATENT TODAY: 9 dirs match the orphan shape (verified: e.g. 430_003_impl_override_only, 365_001_basic_intercept), but all 9 are FAILURE so the gate correctly holds. Flips to alarm the instant one compiles and gets a SUCCESS marker with its expected.txt still unchecked.

commission_queue.title: A behavior-changing fix(...) under src/ must land with a regression test
commission_queue.intent: CONTRIBUTING/AGENTS both mandate failing-test-first; a src/ behavior fix with no tests/ change ships a change with zero pinned evidence.
commission_queue.faucet: FACT: for each `^fix` commit, `git show --name-only`; flag if it touches src/*.zig but no path under tests/. INTENT axis fix_is_test_pinned: +1 the diff adds/updates a regression exercising the fixed path, -1 a behavior-changing fix lands with no test and no stated untestability reason.
commission_queue.gate: fire = FACT(fix touches src/, not tests/) × INTENT(fix_is_test_pinned <= -0.5) × gain >= floor. Judge suppresses docs/snapshot-only fix commits and fixes already covered by an existing re-run test.
commission_queue.fires_on: VERIFIED: b203f6cb `fix(codegen): unbalanced closer...` touches only src/codegen_utils.zig, zero tests/. Control d87beceb `fix(parser): reject unbalanced...` lands with its tests/regression/100_081 — FACT half silent.

watchers.intent: After the canonicalize pass runs, EVERY ast.DottedPath in the program tree has module_qualifier != null (it is the documented post-condition of canonicalize_names.zig).
watchers.trusted_via: a-comment + convention: the post-condition is asserted only in the docstring (src/canonicalize_names.zig:11 'After this pass, ALL DottedPaths have a module_qualifier set'); the walker is a hand-maintained switch and nothing checks the post-condition. Downstream consumers each carry their own `orelse <module_name>` fallback that silently papers over any miss.
watchers.grounding: src/canonicalize_names.zig:43-204 (the hand-written walker over ast.Item/ast.Step — note canonicalizeArg:214 and canonicalizeBranchConstructor:220 are explicit no-ops that skip their subtree); the trust breaks at consumers src/auto_discharge_inserter.zig:586,909,1245,1504 (`path.module_qualifier orelse flow.module`) and worst at src/continuation_codegen.zig:31 (`if (invocation.path.module_qualifier) |mq| {...}` — when null the entire module-prefix block is skipped and a BARE unqualified symbol is emitted).
watchers.faucet_fact: AST-walk src/canonicalize_names.zig: enumerate every ast.Item and ast.Step variant that (transitively) holds a DottedPath field (grep ast.zig for `: DottedPath` / `: ?DottedPath` -> 13 fields across Item/Step/Tap/native_loop/fused/inlined), then check each is reached by a `canonicalizePath` call in the walker. Returns the count of DottedPath-bearing variants NOT covered (today: Arg and BranchConstructor subtrees are explicitly skipped — return >0 if any of those can actually carry a path, else the FACT is 'a new Item/Step variant added since the walker was last edited holds a path with no canonicalizePath call').
watchers.faucet_intent: axis path_coverage_complete: +1 the diff adds/edits a DottedPath-bearing AST variant AND adds the matching canonicalizePath call in the walker (or an explicit, justified skip comment), -1 a new path-bearing variant or field is added with no corresponding walker edit. axis fallback_masks_invariant: +1 a downstream module_qualifier read asserts non-null, -1 it adds another silent `orelse`/`if(mq)` that lets a null slide.
watchers.gate: fire = (FACT: count of uncovered DottedPath-bearing variants >= 1) x (INTENT: path_coverage_complete <= -0.5 on the introducing diff) x gain >= floor. The mechanical coverage count anchors the judge so a benign walker refactor (rename, reorder) that keeps full coverage scores FACT=0 and cannot fire.
watchers.fires_on: A commit that adds a new ast.Item or ast.Step variant carrying a DottedPath without touching src/canonicalize_names.zig — the new path keeps module_qualifier==null, continuation_codegen.zig:31 silently emits an unqualified symbol, and it surfaces three steps later as a mysterious 'unknown symbol' or wrong-module resolution in generated Zig. The two explicit no-op skips (canonicalizeArg:214, canonicalizeBranchConstructor:220) are the standing proof the walker already chooses NOT to descend into some subtrees by hand.
watchers.stays_silent_on: A commit that edits canonicalizePath's separator-normalization (the `/`->`.` loop at :233-238) or renames a walker helper while keeping every DottedPath-bearing variant covered — coverage count stays 0, watcher silent.

watchers.intent: Every ast.DottedPath has a non-empty segments slice — segments[0] (and segments[len-1]) are dereferenced without a length guard across the compiler.
watchers.trusted_via: nothing — pure convention that the parser never emits a zero-segment path. No assertion at the parse boundary, no guard at the read sites.
watchers.grounding: Unguarded reads: src/canonicalize_names.zig:249,251 (`path.segments[0]`), src/compiler_requires.zig:82,88,95 (`flow.invocation.path.segments[0]`), src/auto_discharge_inserter.zig:2586,2594-2595 (`path.segments[0].len`/memcpy), src/ast_functional.zig:3130 (`event.path.segments[0]`), src/ast_serializer.zig:1799,1846 (`segments[segments.len-1]`). Construction site that must uphold it: src/parser.zig:4214-4222 (dup_segments built from event_path.segments — empty in, empty out).
watchers.faucet_fact: grep the compiler for `\.segments\[0\]`, `\.segments\[.*len - 1\]`, and `.segments[0].len` and subtract the count of those reads that are dominated by a preceding `.segments.len > 0` / `!= 0` guard in the same function. Returns the count of UNGUARDED first/last-segment dereferences (today: ~8+, e.g. canonicalize:249 has no guard).
watchers.faucet_intent: axis empty_path_unreachable: +1 a diff that can newly construct a DottedPath proves segments is non-empty at the construction site (literal with >=1 element, or an explicit guard), -1 a diff builds segments from a possibly-empty source (a slice of a parsed list, a split result) and feeds it to a path with no min-length check.
watchers.gate: fire = (FACT: a NEW unguarded segments[0]/[len-1] read introduced, OR a new DottedPath construction from an unchecked-length source) x (INTENT: empty_path_unreachable <= -0.5) x gain >= floor. A pure read added next to an existing guard scores FACT=0.
watchers.fires_on: src/parser.zig:4214 — `parsePassThroughInvocation` dups event_path.segments verbatim; if a parse path ever yields an event_path with zero segments (e.g. a malformed `:` qualifier with nothing after it), the pass-through invocation inherits an empty segments and canonicalize_names.zig:249 indexes segments[0] -> panic with no source location, looking like an internal compiler crash rather than a parse error.
watchers.stays_silent_on: A read like emitter_helpers.zig:4461 `invocation.path.segments[0]` that sits after an established non-empty guarantee, or a refactor that adds a `segments.len` loop — no new unguarded first-element index, watcher silent.

watchers.intent: The parse-time flag is_impl == (event_path.module_qualifier != null) must be captured BEFORE the canonicalize pass runs, because canonicalize unconditionally fills module_qualifier on every path and thereby destroys the 'was this path module-qualified in source?' signal that is_impl/impl_of encode.
watchers.trusted_via: convention + ordering discipline: is_impl is snapshotted at parse time (parser.zig:4199 `.is_impl = event_path.module_qualifier != null`) and is RELIED ON to mean 'source-qualified' long after canonicalize has made module_qualifier non-null everywhere. Nothing prevents a future pass from re-deriving is_impl from module_qualifier post-canonicalize (which would now be universally true), or from re-ordering canonicalize before the snapshot.
watchers.grounding: Snapshot site: src/parser.zig:4199 (`.is_impl = event_path.module_qualifier != null`). Destroyer: src/canonicalize_names.zig:246 (`path.module_qualifier = try ctx.allocator.dupe(...)` — sets it on EVERY previously-null path). Consumers that trust the snapshot: src/ast_serializer.zig:515-516,649-652, src/ast_functional.zig:792,1287,1720,1803,1927 (clone-propagate is_impl), and impl_of-based dispatch in src/ast_transform.zig:133.
watchers.faucet_fact: AST-walk: flag any read of `.module_qualifier != null` (or `== null`) used to derive is_impl / impl-status / cross-module-override semantics that occurs in a pass scheduled AFTER canonicalize in build.zig's pass order. Also flag any new write to `.is_impl`/`.impl_of` not co-located with the parser. Returns count of such post-canonicalize is_impl derivations (today: 0 — the snapshot is correctly the only source).
watchers.faucet_intent: axis impl_signal_pre_canonicalize: +1 is_impl/impl_of is read or set only from the parse-time snapshot and is threaded forward verbatim, -1 a diff re-derives module-qualified-ness from module_qualifier in or after canonicalize (where it is now always non-null, silently making every flow look like an impl).
watchers.gate: fire = (FACT: a `module_qualifier ?== null`-derived impl decision appears in a post-canonicalize pass, OR is_impl is written outside the parser) x (INTENT: impl_signal_pre_canonicalize <= -0.5) x gain >= floor. Cloning that copies `.is_impl = flow.is_impl` verbatim (ast_functional.zig) scores FACT=0 and stays silent.
watchers.fires_on: Not yet broken in the repo — but the trap is loaded: a maintainer adding a new dispatch pass that decides 'is this a cross-module override?' by checking `path.module_qualifier != null` (the natural thing to write) would, post-canonicalize-name:246, find EVERY path qualified and treat every local flow as a cross-module impl. The snapshot at parser.zig:4199 exists precisely because this is non-obvious, and nothing stops the regression.
watchers.stays_silent_on: The existing clones at ast_functional.zig:792 etc. that copy is_impl field-to-field, and the serializer at ast_serializer.zig:516 that emits the snapshotted bool — no post-canonicalize re-derivation, watcher silent.

watchers.intent: Every error code emitted to users as `error[XXX]:` must be a real member of the `ErrorCode` enum in src/errors.zig (the single registry of diagnostic codes).
watchers.trusted_via: convention — the canonical render path errors.zig:121 does `error[{tagName}]` off the enum, so codes are normally impossible to misspell; the one raw hand-formatted emit site is trusted only by reviewer-attention plus a self-flagged `// TODO` the author left in.
watchers.grounding: src/errors.zig:3-79 defines `ErrorCode` (KORU001..KORU121, PARSE001-005, TYPE001-005, SHAPE001-002). src/errors.zig:121 renders `error[{tagName}]`. The drift lives at src/main.zig:3604 which prints literal `error[KORU200]` — KORU200 is NOT in the enum (grep of src/errors.zig confirms absent), and the function returns the WRONG type `error.ModuleNotFound` (main.zig:3614) with a `// TODO: Add proper AmbiguousModule error`.

watchers.faucet_intent: none
watchers.gate: Pure fact gate: fire = |emitted_codes \ enum_members| >= 1. No judge needed — it is a set-difference on a closed registry.
watchers.fires_on: src/main.zig:3604 emits `error[KORU200]` which is absent from the ErrorCode enum at src/errors.zig:3-79. Current HEAD (commit 81d9519c). Non-vacuous: 11 EXPECT regression files assert `CONTAINS error[KORUxxx]` codes, so a future renumber that drops a code would surface here too.

KORU200 is the ONLY raw-string `error[CODE]` literal in src.

watchers.intent: The single example in README.md (the project's front door) must compile and run with the current koruc, since it is the first syntax a new user copies.
watchers.trusted_via: nothing — the README example is plain prose, never run by any test or CI step; it is trusted purely by whoever last remembered to update it after a syntax change.
watchers.grounding: README.md:6-14 shows `~import "$std/io"`, `~greet = greeting "Hello," ++ ...`, and `std.io:print.ln(msg)`. Running `./zig-out/bin/koruc /tmp/<readme>.kz` rejects line 1 with PARSE003 ('imports are bare — drop the `~`') and, after fixing that, rejects the `~greet = greeting ...` subflow with KORU040 'unknown event'. The language moved `~import`→bare `import` (see commit context) and the `:`-namespace to `/`, but README never followed.
watchers.faucet_fact: Extract fenced ```koru blocks from README.md (and optionally koru-tutorial.md / koru-by-example.md), write each to a temp .kz, run `koruc` on it, fire on any non-zero/diagnostic-bearing compile. Returns the failing block + first diagnostic line.
watchers.faucet_intent: none
watchers.gate: Fact gate: fire = (koruc on README example produces a diagnostic / non-success). Deterministic — the compiler is the oracle.
watchers.fires_on: README.md:6-14 — the only example in the file — fails to compile at HEAD: PARSE003 on `~import`, then KORU040 on the `~greet = greeting` subflow. Verified by running the exact snippet through ./zig-out/bin/koruc.
watchers.stays_silent_on: A doc example that DOES match current syntax (e.g. the `import std/io` + subflow forms used in passing tests/regression/*.kz) compiles clean — the watcher stays silent on those, so it is not a blanket 'docs are stale' linter; it fires only when a doc snippet actually breaks against the live compiler.

watchers.intent: Every regression EXPECT file that asserts `CONTAINS error[KORUxxx]` must reference a code the compiler can actually still emit under that name — the test's hardcoded code and the enum/emit site must stay in lockstep.
watchers.trusted_via: a-partial-test — the full ./run_regression.sh run is the only thing that would catch a stale EXPECT code, and only if that specific test is in-scope and actually executed; the code string inside EXPECT is otherwise an untyped literal that nothing validates structurally.
watchers.grounding: scripts/regression_lib.sh:101-124 implements `CONTAINS`/`NOT_CONTAINS` as a literal `grep -qF` against compile_kz.err. 11 EXPECT files assert codes, e.g. tests/regression/100_MODULE_SYSTEM/140_FILE_LAYOUT/140_007_.../EXPECT contains `CONTAINS KORU111`. The asserted code is a free-text substring — if errors.zig renames KORU111 or the emit site changes the number, the grep silently fails (or, worse, the test is SKIP/TODO and never runs).
watchers.faucet_fact: Collect every `CONTAINS error\[([A-Z]+[0-9]+)\]` (and bare `CONTAINS (KORU|PARSE|TYPE|SHAPE)[0-9]+`) code referenced across tests/**/EXPECT into set A. Build enum set R from src/errors.zig. Fire if A - R is non-empty (a test pins a code no longer in the registry). Optionally cross-check A against the set of codes any emit site can actually produce.
watchers.faucet_intent: none
watchers.gate: Fact gate: fire = |EXPECT-referenced codes \ enum_members| >= 1. Closed-registry set difference, deterministic.
watchers.fires_on: Not currently firing on a rename (codes match today), BUT it is the structural guard the project lacks: today the ONLY thing keeping these 11 EXPECT codes honest is running the full suite with those tests in-scope. The KORU200 case (candidate 1) proves codes CAN exist outside the enum — an EXPECT could pin KORU200 today and this watcher would flag it as un-registry-backed. watchers.faucet_intent: axis taught_as_live: +1 the doc presents the token as the current way to do X (imperative example, 'use `~import`'), -1 the doc presents it as removed/historical ('`println` was deleted', struck through). watchers.gate: PRODUCT: fire = (dead_form_grep_count >= 1) × (judge taught_as_live >= +1) — the correct mechanical fact (token IS pinned-dead AND appears in the doc) gates the judge; refuses to fire when the doc only references the dead form to document its removal.
watchers.fires_on: README.md teaches `std.io:print.ln` (dot namespace) and `~import "$std/io"` as the live hello-world — both pinned-dead forms presented imperatively. taught_as_live = +1, grep_count >= 1 → fires.
watchers.stays_silent_on: 010_054's own input.kz keeps `~std/io:println(...)` but is a MUST_FAIL negative test with 'codemod:skip — negative test' header; a prose line like 'the old `println` was removed in favor of print.ln' scores taught_as_live = -1 → product is 0 → silent.

watchers.intent: Every doc file, build command, or test number a governance/protocol doc tells contributors to update or run MUST actually exist — a referenced target that is gone is a discipline nothing can follow.
watchers.trusted_via: convention / reviewer-attention only — CONTRIBUTING.md prescribes a 5-step 'Documentation Update Protocol' and a PR checklist, but no CI, hook, or test verifies the referenced files exist or the commands resolve.
watchers.grounding: CONTRIBUTING.md:18-37 (update SPEC.md, KORU.md, STATUS.md, docs/development/TEST_DOCUMENTATION_MAP.md), :45-52 (KNOWN_ISSUES.md), :211/:238 ('verified by test 123', 'test 405'). Verified MISSING on disk: SPEC.md, KORU.md, STATUS.md, TEST_DOCUMENTATION_MAP.md, KNOWN_ISSUES.md, DOCUMENTATION.md, AI.md. AGENTS.md:48 prescribes `npm run status` — no root package.json defines a 'status' script (verified absent).
watchers.faucet_fact: Parse governance docs (CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md) for (a) referenced repo-relative file paths, (b) `npm run X` / `node scripts/X` commands, (c) `test NNN` / `(test NNN)` references. For each: stat the file / resolve the npm script in package.json / confirm a regression dir matching NNN exists. Returns count of dangling references with their CONTRIBUTING.md:line.
watchers.faucet_intent: none
watchers.gate: fact alone: fire when dangling_reference_count >= 1. Deterministic existence check — no judge.
watchers.fires_on: CONTRIBUTING.md's entire Documentation Update Protocol points at SPEC.md / KORU.md / STATUS.md / TEST_DOCUMENTATION_MAP.md / KNOWN_ISSUES.md — all confirmed MISSING. AGENTS.md:48 `npm run status` does not resolve (no root package.json). The protocol is unfollowable as written.
watchers.stays_silent_on: A reference to README.md, build.zig, run_regression.sh, or tests/regression/ (all present) does not fire; a `(test 405)` whose directory exists does not fire — the watcher only flags the dead targets, not the live ones.

watchers.intent: A doc claim of the form 'X works (verified by test NNN)' / 'Last Verified: DATE (test NNN)' must point at a test that (a) exists and (b) actually exercises X — the verification-receipt discipline CONTRIBUTING preaches must not decay into a bare citation nobody re-checks.
watchers.trusted_via: a-comment / convention — CONTRIBUTING.md:60-64 and :209-215 mandate 'Add Verification Date / Note which tests verify the claim / Format: Last Verified: YYYY-MM-DD (test NNN)', but no mechanism confirms the cited test number resolves or that the doc date isn't stale relative to the test's last change.
watchers.grounding: CONTRIBUTING.md:62-64 ('Last Verified: 2025-10-02 (test 401-405)'), :150-154 (Monthly audit: 'Check SPEC.md examples compile / Verify KORU.md tutorials work'). The audit is prescribed as a MANUAL monthly maintainer chore (CONTRIBUTING.md:136 'Maintainers should run this monthly') — i.e. trusted to human discipline, watched by nothing.
watchers.faucet_fact: grep all docs for `verified by test N`, `(test N)`, `Last Verified: <date> (test N)`. For each citation: confirm a tests/regression dir for N exists; if a date is present, compare it against `git log -1 --format=%cd` of that test's input.kz — flag when the test changed AFTER the doc's Last-Verified date (claim is stale) or when N does not resolve. Returns stale/dangling citation count + file:line.
watchers.faucet_intent: axis claim_still_holds: +1 the cited test plausibly exercises the documented feature (name/cluster matches the claim), -1 the citation is decorative or the test is unrelated to the prose claim around it. Used only to suppress benign number-mentions that aren't verification claims.
watchers.gate: PRODUCT: fire = (citation_resolves_and_date_is_stale-or-dangling : fact) × (claim_still_holds judge != irrelevant). The mechanical staleness/dangling fact is primary; the judge keeps it from firing on a passing mention of a number that isn't a verification receipt.
watchers.fires_on: CONTRIBUTING.md:211 cites 'verified by test 123' and :238 'test 405' as exemplars; if treated as live receipts neither maps to a present descriptively-named regression dir (regressions are NNN_name dirs, not bare 123/405) — dangling citation, fires. (Also any future 'Last Verified' whose test was edited after the date.)
watchers.stays_silent_on: koru-by-example.json topic configs reference real cluster ids (000_CORE_LANGUAGE etc.) that the corpus generator already validates and which resolve on disk — those stay silent; a citation whose test exists and whose Last-Verified date is newer than the test's last edit stays silent.
